context.process_name: Expense Processing: T&E Review & Scrubbing (AEA Variant)
context.objective: Document how we carry out Expense Processing: T&E Review & Scrubbing (AEA Variant), the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we add the report to the review tracker. What we do: record cardholder, statement total, submitted amount, report identifier, and status; add fields for PDF saved, receipts, two approvals, exceptions, and completion; compare statement and submitted totals and flag a difference.
What prompts you to add an expense report to the review tracker?

Next, we validate receipts and personal-expense classification. What we do: confirm the current receipt threshold and personal-expense exception before applying them; check each line against the validated rule; flag missing receipt or questionable personal classification to the submitter/client; record resolution in the tracker.
What tells you that a missing receipt or questionable personal-expense classification has been resolved?

After that, we validate approvals and keep report records. What we do: confirm the current required number/types of approvals; verify approvers/statuses in Concur; capture and save approval screenshots because no record is available through the API; save the report PDF and update tracker flags.
What happens when Concur shows an approval is missing or its status is not valid?

Then, we close report-level exceptions. What we do: communicate each receipt, approval, amount, or classification exception; retain response/correction; update status only after the source report or approved exception support is complete.
For an amount exception, what needs to be corrected or documented for the source report or approved exception support to count as complete?

Once that is done, we receive and validate the macro batch. What we do: receive the AEA-generated raw export split into LP, SBF, Growth, and Debt; record macro version/export date where available; reconcile report count and total dollars in the batch to the cleared Concur/tracker population; resolve missing, duplicate, or entity-split differences.
What happens to the batch after the report counts and total dollars reconcile?

Following that, we review coding and descriptions under confirmed rules. What we do: review entity and general ledger coding against the client rulebook; apply the confirmed description format and required components; apply confirmed lunch and dinner maximums, and document any split between the billable amount and the individual or management company excess; do not apply the transportation timing rule until the 7:30pm/7:00am wording is corrected and approved. Flag affected lines; record every manual change and exception.
What happens to flagged transportation lines while the wording awaits correction and approval?

Following that, we net eligible refund/charge pairs. What we do: match refund and charge by the approved identifiers and period; net only same-period pairs meeting the confirmed criteria; keep both source lines and the netting calculation; flag pairs from different periods or ambiguous pairs. Do not offset them based on an assumption.
What happens to pairs flagged as being from different periods or ambiguous?

Following that, we review and route the clean batch. What we do: compare clean-batch totals with the raw batch and explain approved splits and netting; review entity, coding, descriptions, receipts, approvals, and exception closure; route the approved batch for posting; route billable fund/portfolio-company lines to and reconcile the handoff; retain the final package and approval.
Who approves the clean batch before it is routed for posting?

notes.summary: The team reviews the clean batch against the raw batch, routes the approved batch for posting, and reconciles the billable-line handoff. Who receives the billable fund and portfolio-company lines?
